Greg Abbott (born November 13, 1957) is an American politician, attorney, and jurist who has served since 2015 as the 48th governor of Texas.
This German chancellor's 16-year tenure — the longest in the country's post-war history — spanned the end of the Cold War, German reunification, and the founding of the European Union — who is he?
Helmut Kohl (3 April 1930 - 16 June 2017) was a German politician who served as chancellor of Germany and governed the Federal Republic from 1982 to 1998.
This Venezuelan leader renamed his country the "Bolivarian Republic" and gave his name to a whole political ideology before dying in office in 2013 — who was he?
Hugo Chávez (28 July 1954 - 5 March 2013) was a Venezuelan politician, revolutionary, and military officer who was the president of Venezuela from 1999 until his death in 2013.

Jack Carter (politician) (born July 3, 1947) is an American businessman, politician and environmentalist.

Jim Mattis (born September 8, 1950) is an American military officer who served as the 26th United States secretary of defense from 2017 to 2019.
A mountain range on Pluto and an asteroid both bear her name — fitting for the Japanese climber who was the first woman atop Everest and the first to bag the Seven Summits. Who was she?
Junko Tabei (ne Ishibashi; 22 September 1939 - 20 October 2016) was a Japanese mountaineer, author and teacher.

William Lever, 1st Viscount Leverhulme: English industrialist, philanthropist and politician (1851–1925)

Founded in 2012 by former TV journalist Yair Lapid, this centrist Israeli party placed second with 19 Knesset seats in its debut election and later co-founded the short-lived Blue and White alliance in 2019 — which party?
Yesh Atid: Israeli political party. Yesh Atid (Hebrew: יֵשׁ עָתִיד, lit. 'There is a Future') is a centrist political party in Israel.
Who wrote The Emperor's New Clothes?

The Emperor's New Clothes → Hans Christian Andersen. The tale has been translated into over 100 languages.

Who among these was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Bash (Unix shell) (founded 1989) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was established earliest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is a physicist?
Which of these is a chemist?
Ellen Swallow Richards is a chemist. Richards graduated from Westford Academy (second oldest secondary school in Massachusetts) in 1862.
What is the atomic number of Moscovium?
Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
What is the atomic number of Bismuth?
Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
In what year did Marie Curie die?
Marie Curie: Curie was born in Warsaw, Russian Empire, where she studied at the clandestine Flying University and began her practical scientific training.
In what year was Sodium discovered?
Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
Ammonium chloride: Pfizer. Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as [NH4]Cl.
Boeing 777X: United States. The Boeing 777X is an American long-range, wide-body, twin-engine airliner built by Boeing Commercial Airplanes, undergoing flight testing.
Who is credited with discovering Telescopium?
Telescopium: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Its name is a Latinized form of the Greek word for telescope.
Who is credited with discovering Spontaneous generation?
Spontaneous generation: Anaximander. It was hypothesized that certain forms, such as fleas, could arise from inanimate matter such as dust, or that maggots could arise from dead flesh.
Who is credited with discovering SN 1987A?
SN 1987A: Ian Shelton. SN 1987A was a Type II supernova in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a dwarf satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.
This Onmyōdō master advised Heian emperors on astrology and spiritual matters; a Kyoto shrine and an Osaka train station now honor him — who is he?
Abe no Seimei (February 21, 921 AD - October 31, 1005) was a Japanese onmyji, a court official and specialist of Onmyd, during the middle of the Heian period.
First approved in the United States in 1966, this xanthine oxidase inhibitor treats high uric acid levels linked to gout, kidney stones, and chemotherapy — what medication is it?
Allopurinol is a medication used to decrease high blood uric acid levels.
Nicknamed 'the heart of the scorpion,' this distinctly reddish variable star is the brightest in the constellation Scorpius — what is it?
Antares is the brightest star in the constellation of Scorpius. It has the Bayer designation α Scorpii, which is Latinised to Alpha Scorpii.

Named for the Ancient Greek word for 'star' after its flower shape, this group of roughly 170 mostly Eurasian perennial plants is also known for its late-blooming 'Michaelmas daisies' — which plant group?
Aster (genus) is a genus of perennial flowering plants in the family Asteraceae.
Once chairman of the Nasdaq, this financier admitted to masterminding the largest-known Ponzi scheme in history, estimated at $65 billion — who was he?

Bernie Madoff (April 29, 1938 - April 14, 2021) was an American financier, con artist, and stock broker who was the admitted mastermind of the largest-known Ponzi scheme in history, worth an estimated $65 billion.
This family of cloven-hoofed, ruminant mammals includes cattle, bison, buffalo, antelopes, sheep, and goats across 143 living species — name the family?
Bovidae is the biological family of cloven-hoofed, ruminant mammals that includes cattle, bison, buffalo, antelopes, and goat-antelopes such as sheep and goats.
Sole living family in the mammalian suborder Tylopoda, which group unites camels with llamas and their South American relatives?
Camelidae is a family of mammals belonging to the ungulate order Artiodactyla (even-toed ungulates) and the only living family in the suborder Tylopoda.
A secondarily aquatic clade within the order that also includes hippos, this infraorder covers whales, dolphins and porpoises, along with extinct relatives like Basilosaurus — which group of animals?

Cetacean are marine mammals belonging to the infraorder Cetacea, a secondarily aquatic clade under the order Artiodactyla that include whales, dolphins, porpoises and extinct groups such as Basilosaurus.

From a tree in the myrtle family, these dried flower buds from the Moluccas are harvested year-round across different countries and lend their scent to everything from cosmetics to cooking — what are they?
Clove are the aromatic flower buds of a tree in the family Myrtaceae, Syzygium aromaticum.

This naturally occurring but largely inactive steroid hormone shields organs like the kidneys from active cortisol, and gets converted back into cortisol by an enzyme mainly in the liver — what hormone is it?
Cortisone is a naturally occurring, mostly inactive pregnene (21-carbon) steroid hormone.
The word names both a noun — a plan or proposal made by a thinking agent — and a verb for developing one, always aiming to satisfy goals while weighing function and aesthetics; what is it?
Design is the concept or proposal for an object, process, or system.
This soil-dwelling invertebrate of the phylum Annelida is also known by slang names like 'dew-worm,' 'rainworm,' and 'nightcrawler.' What creature is it?
Earthworm is a soil-dwelling terrestrial invertebrate that belongs to the phylum Annelida.

A German Jew who fled the Nazi regime for the United States, this social psychologist and psychoanalyst co-founded a New York psychiatric institute and was associated with the Frankfurt School of critical theory — who is he?
Erich Fromm (March 23, 1900 - March 18, 1980) was a German-American social psychologist, psychoanalyst, sociologist, humanistic philosopher, and democratic socialist.
Bred in Brazil as a guard dog, cattle herder, and big-game hunter, this large mastiff-type breed was also once used to catch runaway slaves — which breed?
Fila Brasileiro (Portuguese) is a Brazilian breed of large working dog of mastiff type.

Cataloged by the astronomer Ptolemy in the second century AD and still one of the 88 modern constellations, this zodiac constellation takes its Latin name from the mythological twins Castor and Pollux — what's the constellation?
Gemini (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the northern celestial hemisphere.

Native to the Amazon basin, this climbing plant's coffee-bean-sized seeds can contain up to 6% caffeine — roughly double the concentration found in green coffee beans — and flavor a popular Brazilian soft drink. Name the plant?
Guarana (from the Portuguese guaran; Paullinia cupana, syns.

This colorless, nearly odorless organic compound is a straight-chain alkane with six carbon atoms, widely used as a cheap, largely unreactive solvent and found in small amounts in modern gasoline blends — what is it?
Hexane is an organic compound, a straight-chain alkane with six carbon atoms and the molecular formula C6H14.
This medical condition occurs when the body, or a region of it, is deprived of adequate oxygen at the tissue level — what is it called?

Hypoxia (medicine) is a condition in which the body or a region of the body is deprived of an adequate oxygen supply at the tissue level. Hypoxia may be classified as either generalized, affecting the whole body, or local, affecting a region of the body.

This English mathematician made foundational contributions to matrix and invariant theory, founded the American Journal of Mathematics at Johns Hopkins, and was teaching at Oxford when he died. Who was he?
James Joseph Sylvester (3 September 1814 - 15 March 1897) was an English mathematician.

The first woman of Indian origin to fly to space, this astronaut and aerospace engineer first studied in India before earning advanced degrees in the US and flying aboard Space Shuttle Columbia in 1997 — who was she?
Kalpana Chawla (July 1, 1962 - February 1, 2003) was an Indian-American astronaut and aerospace engineer who was the first woman of Indian origin to fly to space.
This small Arctic rodent is a key prey source for tundra carnivores and is the subject of a persistent myth that it marches off cliffs in mass suicide — what animal is it?
Lemming is a small rodent, usually found in or near the Arctic in tundra biomes.
Named for a Dutch physicist, this six-parameter family of linear equations converts spacetime coordinates between reference frames moving at constant relative velocity — what is it?
Lorentz transformation are a six-parameter family of linear transformations from a coordinate frame in spacetime to another frame that moves at a constant velocity relative to the former.

A student of Marie Curie, this French physicist discovered a new element in 1939 by purifying lanthanum laced with actinium, and went on to become the first woman elected to the French Académie des Sciences — who was she?
Marguerite Perey (19 October 1909 - 13 May 1975) was a French physicist and a student of Marie Curie.

This American theoretical physicist and science communicator, a professor at the City College of New York, won a 2021 lifetime achievement award named for a famous science-fiction author, honoring his work bridging science and sci-fi. Who is he?
Michio Kaku (born January 24, 1947) is an American theoretical physicist, science communicator, futurologist, and writer of popular science.
Scholars can't even agree on which elements define it, yet it appears in every human society as a vehicle for creativity through composition and performance — what is it?
Music is the arrangement of sound to create some combination of form, harmony, melody, rhythm, or otherwise expressive content.
A highly corrosive mineral compound with the formula HNO3, this strong inorganic acid is colorless but yellows over time as it decomposes. What is this acid?
Nitric acid is an inorganic compound with the formula HNO3. The compound is colorless, but samples tend to acquire a yellow cast over time due to decomposition into oxides of nitrogen.
This systemic skeletal disorder develops when the rate of bone breakdown outpaces new bone formation with age, leaving bones porous, less dense, and prone to fracture — what's the condition called?
Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disorder characterized by low bone mass, micro-architectural deterioration of bone tissue leading to more porous bone, and consequent increase in fracture risk.
Brought on by too little niacin, this disease announces itself with the 'three D's' — dermatitis on sun-exposed skin, diarrhea, and dementia — what is it?
Pellagra is a disease caused by a lack of the vitamin niacin (vitamin B3).
Which condition, more common in people with obesity or a family history, involves hair and skin debris being drawn into tissue through tiny skin openings called pits?
Pilonidal disease is a type of skin infection that typically occurs as a cyst between the cheeks of the buttocks and often at the upper end.

This corticosteroid drug treats a huge range of conditions — from rheumatoid arthritis and asthma to eye inflammation and certain cancers — and can be taken orally, injected, or applied to the skin. What is it?
Prednisolone is a corticosteroid, a steroid hormone used to treat certain types of allergies, inflammatory conditions, autoimmune disorders, and cancers, electrolyte imbalances, and skin conditions.
This root vegetable in the mustard family, whose entire plant (leaves included) is edible, was domesticated in Asia and is now grown worldwide — what vegetable is it?
Radish (Raphanus sativus or Raphanus raphanistrum subsp.
This big, sociable black corvid is told apart from its relatives by a bare, whitish patch on its face, and it nests in noisy treetop colonies near farms and villages — which bird is it?
Rook (bird) (Corvus frugilegus) is a member of the family Corvidae in the passerine order of birds.

These pinnipeds, distinguished from true seals by their external ear flaps and ability to walk on all fours, belong to the eared-seal family alongside fur seals, with six living species worldwide. What animal is this?
Sea lion are pinnipeds characterized by external ear flaps, long foreflippers, the ability to walk on all fours, short and thick hair, and a big chest and belly.

Named from an Ancient Greek word for 'soap,' this cheesy secretion of shed skin cells, oils, and moisture collects under the foreskin in males and around the folds of female genitalia — what is it called?
Smegma (from Ancient Greek, smgma, 'soap') is a cheesy substance composed of shed skin cells, skin oils, and moisture that occurs in male and female mammalian genitalia.
A Canadian cognitive psychologist at Harvard who champions evolutionary psychology and the computational theory of mind, which popular-science author wrote on how children learn irregular verb forms?
Steven Pinker (born September 18, 1954) is a Canadian cognitive psychologist, psycholinguist, popular science author, and public intellectual.
This protective cap of repetitive nucleotide sequences guards the ends of eukaryotic chromosomes from progressive degradation — what is it called?
Telomere (from Ancient Greek (tlos) 'end' and (mros) 'part') is a region of repetitive nucleotide sequences associated with specialized proteins at the ends of linear chromosomes (see Sequences).
Divided into the thorax, abdomen, and pelvis, this core section of the body is where the head, neck, and all four limbs attach — which body part?
Torso is the central part, or the core, of the body of many animals (including human beings), from which the head, neck, limbs, tail and other appendages extend.
Measuring under five feet long, this critically endangered porpoise is endemic to a small corner of Mexico's Baja California coast — which species?
Vaquita (v-; Phocoena sinus) is a species of porpoise endemic to the northern end of the Gulf of California in Baja California, Mexico.
Inspired by the code-breaking game Mastermind, this once-a-day puzzle gives you six tries and colored tiles to crack the same word everyone else is solving — which game?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Wordle is a web-based word game created and developed by the Welsh software engineer Josh Wardle.

This organic compound functions as a neurotransmitter in the brain and body of many animal types, including humans. It is the chemical that motor neurons release at the neuromuscular junction to enable muscle movement. What is it?
Acetylcholine: Organic chemical and neurotransmitter. Its name is derived from its chemical structure: it is an ester of acetic acid and choline.
Born in 1929 and died in 2001, this man was a respected Saudi Islamic scholar — who is he?

Native to South Africa's Western Cape, this flowering bulb genus lends its common name to popular winter houseplants that actually belong to a different genus, Hippeastrum — which bulb, also called the naked lady or Jersey lily?
Amaryllis: Genus of plants. Amaryllis is the only genus in the subtribe Amaryllidinae (tribe Amaryllideae).
Named from Greek words for 'curved' and 'vertebra,' this type of arthritis causes long-term inflammation where the spine meets the pelvis — what is it?
Ankylosing spondylitis: Type of arthritis of the spine. Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a type of arthritis from the disease spectrum of axial spondyloarthritis.
Known commonly as palms, this family of over 2,600 flowering plant species includes climbers, shrubs, and tree-like forms mostly found in the tropics — what's the family called?
Arecaceae: Palm family of flowering plants.
The famous AL 288-1 skeleton nicknamed 'Lucy,' unearthed in Ethiopia's Afar region, belongs to which extinct East African hominin species that lived roughly 3.9 to 2.9 million years ago?
Australopithecus afarensis: Extinct hominid from the Pliocene of East Africa.
Sharing its engine, transmission, and rotor system with the Huey utility helicopter, this rapidly-developed attack chopper became America's dedicated gunship escort in the Vietnam War — what is it?
Bell AH-1 Cobra: Family of attack helicopters.

A French child prodigy who wrote a treatise on conic sections at 16, then built one of the first mechanical calculators and traded letters with Fermat that helped birth probability theory — who was he?
Created in 1993 by Swiss student Urban Müller, this esoteric programming language uses just eight simple commands and is often cited as a 'Turing tarpit' — what is it called?
Brainfuck: Esoteric, minimalist programming language. While Brainfuck is fully Turing-complete, it is not intended for practical use but to challenge and amuse programmers.
Discovered in 1817 simultaneously by two German chemists as an impurity in zinc carbonate, this soft silvery-white metal shares chemical traits with zinc and mercury — which element?
Cadmium: Chemical element with atomic number 48 (Cd)
Called the 'father of modern taxonomy,' which Swedish biologist formalized the two-name system for naming living things and was later ennobled as von Linné?
Carl Linnaeus: Swedish biologist and physician (1707–1778)
First flown in 1955 as a tricycle-gear evolution of an earlier taildragger model, this four-seat high-wing aircraft is the most-produced plane in history — which model is it?
Cessna 172: Propeller driven single engine aircraft.
Add this steely-grey transition metal (atomic number 24) to steel and you get stainless; polish it and it reflects nearly 70% of visible light without tarnishing. Which element is it?
Chromium: Chemical element with atomic number 24 (Cr)
Also known as ubiquinone, this antioxidant cofactor helps mitochondria produce ATP and gets its name from ten isoprenyl units in its molecular tail — what is it?
Coenzyme Q10: Biochemical cofactor and antioxidant. Coenzyme Q (CoQ), also known as ubiquinone, is a naturally occurring biochemical cofactor (coenzyme) and an antioxidant produced by the human body.
Found only in placental mammals, this roughly four-inch bundle of 200 to 300 million nerve fibers is the brain's largest white-matter structure, linking its left and right hemispheres — what is it?
Corpus callosum: White matter tract connecting the two cerebral hemispheres.
This herpesvirus genus's human species can cause mononucleosis in adults but birth defects affecting the eyes, ears, liver, and spleen when passed to a fetus — which virus?
Cytomegalovirus: Genus of viruses. The 11 species in this genus include Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV, HHV-5), which is the species that infects humans.
Marked by up to 20 liters of dilute urine a day and intense thirst that drinking barely satisfies, this condition comes in four types tied to problems with the hormone vasopressin — what is it?
Diabetes insipidus: Condition characterized by large amounts of dilute urine and increased thirst.
Working alongside biochemist Katalin Karikó on nucleoside base modifications, this University of Pennsylvania immunologist shared the 2023 Nobel Prize for enabling COVID-19 mRNA vaccines — who is he?
Drew Weissman: American physician and immunologist (born 1959)
First described in 1821, this family of large herbivorous mammals features a snout modified into a trunk and includes extinct relatives such as mammoths — which taxonomic family?
Elephantidae: Family of mammals. The family was first described by John Edward Gray in 1821, and later assigned to taxonomic ranks within the order Proboscidea.

Arising in the food pipe that runs between the throat and the stomach, this disease's two main subtypes are a squamous-cell form common in the developing world and a glandular form more common in developed nations. What is it?
Esophageal cancer: Malignant neoplastic disease of the esophagus.
Carried out by the lungs, kidneys, and skin in vertebrates, this bodily process rids the body of metabolic byproducts like urea, carbon dioxide, and uric acid — what is it called?
Excretion: Elimination of metabolic waste products by an organism.

Sometimes nicknamed a 'cat' though it's actually the sole living member of its own genus in the weasel family, this North American forest mammal has been trapped for its fur since the 1700s — what is it?
Fisher (animal): Species of small, carnivorous mammal native to North America.

Unlike plants, this kingdom of life can't photosynthesize, and unlike most things, it has chitin in its cell walls — feeding instead by oozing digestive enzymes out and absorbing what dissolves. What group includes yeasts, molds, and mushrooms?
Fungus: Organism belonging to kingdom Fungi.
Endemic to China and sporting a handy 'thumb' on its forepaw to grip bamboo, this black-and-white bear weighs in around 100 to 115 kg — what animal is it?
Giant panda: Species of bear. The giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca), also known as the panda bear or simply panda, is a bear species endemic to China.
This large, widely distributed white wading bird nests in colonies built in trees near water and is now expanding its range into northern Europe — which species?
Great egret: Species of bird. The great egret (Ardea alba), also known as the common egret, large egret, great white egret, or great white heron, is a large, widely distributed egret.

Recognizable by V-shaped nostrils and a layer of blubber that keeps it warm in Arctic and temperate coastal waters, this pinniped is the most widely distributed of its kind and can weigh up to 370 pounds — which species?
Harbor seal: Species of pinniped. Blubber under the seal's skin helps to maintain body temperature.

Bred by Polynesians in the pre-Columbian era from two Pacific island species, this tropical flowering plant is the national flower of Malaysia and the unofficial national flower of Haiti — what is it?
Hibiscus × rosa-sinensis: Hybrid species of flowering plant. It is widely cultivated as an ornamental plant in the tropics and subtropics.
Carl Wilhelm Scheele pinned down this gas's composition in 1777; it's flammable, smells of rotten eggs, and kills by blocking cellular respiration much like cyanide — what colorless compound is it?
Hydrogen sulfide: Poisonous and flammable gas. Hydrogen sulfide (preferred IUPAC name and American English) or hydrogen sulphide (Commonwealth English) is a chemical compound with the formula H2S.

His 1962 book The Calculus of Consent launched a theory of how politicians' and bureaucrats' self-interest shapes their decisions, earning him the 1986 Nobel in economics — which founder of public choice theory is this?
James M. Buchanan: American economist and Nobel Laureate (1919–2013)
Dubbed the 'Angel of Death,' this German physician held doctorates in both anthropology and medicine before joining the SS and selecting Auschwitz prisoners for the gas chambers — who was he?
Josef Mengele: Nazi SS doctor at Auschwitz (1911–1979)
Also called German turnip despite not being related to true turnips, this stout cabbage cultivar can be eaten raw or cooked, stem and leaves alike — what vegetable?
Kohlrabi: Biennial cultivar of wild cabbage.
Also known as Peruvian ginseng, this Andean root crop is grown at high altitude in Peru and Bolivia and exported worldwide as a dietary powder — what plant is it?
Lepidium meyenii: Plant species native to South America.
Developed under Kelly Johnson's Skunk Works team after the discovery of Germany's Me 262, this aircraft became the first jet fighter flown operationally by U.S. forces in World War II — which jet?
Lockheed P-80 Shooting Star: First jet aircraft in U.S. operational service.
Known historically as 'magnesia alba' to distinguish it from a manganese-containing mineral called 'magnesia nigra,' this white hygroscopic solid has the formula MgO — what is it?
Magnesium oxide: Chemical compound naturally occurring as periclase.
Widely brewed as a calming herbal tea despite limited clinical evidence for its effects, this annual plant in the daisy family goes by the nickname 'scented mayweed' — which plant?
Matricaria chamomilla: Species of flowering plant.
Marketed under brand names like Quaalude and Sopor, this sedative was pulled from commercial production in the mid-1980s due to widespread misuse — which drug?
Most under a millimeter long, these eight-legged arachnids include the parasite that plagues honeybee colonies and the species behind scabies in humans — what are they?
Considered a cultural universal present in every human society, this medium arranges sound into harmony, melody, and rhythm through composition, improvisation, and performance — what is it?
Music: Form of art using sound.
Erected by entomologist Francis Walker back in 1855, this genus of moths belongs to the family Lasiocampidae — which genus?
This biochemical process lets an organism turn food and water into energy and building blocks, and can go wrong with too much or too little of certain essential substances — what process?
Nutrition: Provision to cells and organisms to support life.
This Romanian-American engineer served as Team Principal of the Alpine Formula One team from February 2022 to July 2023 — who is he?
Otmar Szafnauer: American-Romanian engineer, F1 team lead.
From the Greek for 'the study of disease,' this medical field diagnoses illness largely by analyzing tissue and cell samples — what is it?
Pathology: Study of disease. The word pathology also refers to the study of disease in general, incorporating a wide range of biology research fields and medical practices.
Found naturally in chocolate — especially after fermentation — this trace amine stimulates the central nervous system by binding to a receptor called TAAR1. What compound is it?
Phenethylamine: Organic compound, a stimulant in humans.
Native to Eurasia and temperate Africa but now naturalized worldwide, this flowering plant shares a common name with a banana-like fruit despite being unrelated to it — which species?
Plantago major: Species of flowering plant in the plantain family Plantaginaceae.
Covering the front part of the frontal lobe, this brain region orchestrates higher-order thinking including focus, decision-making, and impulse control — what is it?
Prefrontal cortex: Part of the brain responsible for personality, decision-making, and social behavior.
Emitting beams of radiation from its magnetic poles like a cosmic lighthouse, this highly magnetized, rapidly rotating neutron star produces remarkably precise, repeating pulses — what is it?
Pulsar: Type of neutron star with beams of radiation.

A canine native to the southeastern United States, intermediate in size between the coyote and gray wolf. For a century its status as a separate species has been debated — some call it a coywolf. Name this animal.
Red wolf: Canid native to the southeastern United States. Fish and Wildlife Service recognizes the red wolf as an endangered species and grants it protected status.

He dreamed up an "impossible" triangle, traded ideas with M. C. Escher, and shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics for proving black holes are a robust prediction of general relativity — who is this English mathematician?
Roger Penrose: English mathematician, mathematical physicist (born 1931)
This Taiwanese-American physicist shared the 1976 Nobel Prize with Burton Richter for discovering the subatomic J/ψ particle. Who is he?
Samuel C. C. Ting: Nobel prize winning physicist.
The sole living species in its genus, this coastal California evergreen is the tallest tree species on Earth, reaching over 116 meters and living 2,200 years or more. What is it?
Sequoia sempervirens: Species of tree. Sequoia sempervirens is the sole living species of the genus Sequoia in the cypress family Cupressaceae (formerly treated in Taxodiaceae).

Named in 1842 from Brazilian fossils and often called a saber-toothed tiger despite no close kinship to true tigers, this genus of prehistoric predator roamed the Americas until the early Holocene — which animal?
Smilodon: Extinct genus of saber-toothed cat.
It's the largest order of reptiles — lizards and snakes alike — set apart by horny scales they periodically shed and a hinged upper jaw that lets snakes gape around big prey. Which order?
Squamata: Order of reptiles. The now-extinct mosasaurs reached lengths over 14 m (46 ft).
A sphere of plasma heated to incandescence by nuclear fusion in its core, it radiates mostly visible light and infrared — plus about 10% as what?
The Sun is a massive sphere of hot plasma heated by nuclear fusion in its core, radiating energy mainly as visible light and infrared radiation, with about 10% at ultraviolet energies.
The earliest known example was the stone tool, and the later control of fire is even credited with helping grow the human brain and spark language — what broad field is being described?
Technology: Use of knowledge for practical goals.

About 70% of people infected with this parasite-caused sexually transmitted infection show no symptoms at all, though it can raise the risk of contracting HIV — what condition is it?
Trichomoniasis: Medical condition. Trichomoniasis (trich) is an infectious disease caused by the parasite Trichomonas vaginalis.
Formed by the fusion of membrane vesicles, this shapeless organelle in plant and fungal cells is basically a water-filled storage sac that can even hold engulfed solids. What is it?
Vacuole: Membrane-bound organelle in cells containing fluid.
Descended from a wild bovine ancestor, this large domesticated animal from the Indian subcontinent now also grazes fields in Italy, the Balkans, and Australia — what is it?
Water buffalo: Species of large bovine. The wild water buffalo (Bubalus arnee) is most probably the ancestor of the domestic water buffalo.
Based on how long Earth takes to orbit the Sun, this unit of time comes in tropical and sidereal forms differing by about 20 minutes, with leap years keeping our calendar in sync — what unit?

Year: Unit of time based on Earth's orbit. In scientific use, the tropical year (approximately 365 solar days, 5 hours, 48 minutes, 45 seconds) and the sidereal year (about 20 minutes longer) are more exact.
